=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text tperm "Perm: ["
text tsign "] Sign: "
text tcomma ", "
global perm ulong 8
global dir long 8
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emiti writes a signed n; the magnitude is taken as a ulong so the minimum long cannot overflow
fn emiti n long to void
if lt n 0
emit minus
emitu add bitcast ulong not n 1
else
emitu ulong n
end
end
note Steinhaus-Johnson-Trotter with Even's speedup: every element has a direction (all start left);
note the largest mobile element (one whose neighbour in its direction is smaller) swaps that way, and
note every larger element turns round; each step is one swap, so the sign alternates
fn mobile n ulong to ulong
b = n
for i ulong n
j = add long i get dir i
if and ge j 0 lt j long n
if gt get perm i get perm ulong j
if or eq b n gt get perm i get perm b
b = i
end
end
end
end
ret b
end
fn show n ulong s long to void
emit tperm
for i ulong n
if gt i 0
emit tcomma
end
emitu get perm i
end
emit tsign
emiti s
emit nl
end
fn sjt n ulong to void
for i ulong n
put perm i add i 1
put dir i -1
end
s = long 1
show n s
note each pass makes one new permutation and n! of them end the run: 720 = 6! covers n up to 6
while true bound 720
m = mobile n
if eq m n
break
end
v = get perm m
j = ulong add long m get dir m
put perm m get perm j
put perm j v
t = get dir m
put dir m get dir j
put dir j t
for i ulong n
if gt get perm i v
put dir i neg get dir i
end
end
s = neg s
show n s
end
end
note n = 3 and n = 4: 3! + 4! = 30 lines; 6! = 720 bounds the loop for any n up to 6
fn main to int
sjt 3
emit nl
sjt 4
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
